questions.question: Q1. Why does the classical Flory-Rehner equation underestimate the swelling of an ionic gel such as PAA?

answers.a: Because it overestimates the elastic term.
answers.b: Because it contains no electrostatic (Donnan) term, which provides a large extra osmotic pressure in polyelectrolyte gels.
answers.c: Because it assumes the gel is dry.
answers.d: Because it uses the wrong solvent molar volume.

explanations.a: Incorrect - the elastic term is not the source of the error.
explanations.b: Correct - the classical equation ignores the Donnan osmotic pressure, so ionic-gel swelling is underestimated by 2-5x.
explanations.d: Incorrect - the solvent molar volume is not the issue.

questions.question: Q2. As crosslink density increases (V_e decreases), the equilibrium swelling ratio Q:

answers.b: Decreases, because the elastic retraction term grows.

explanations.b: Correct - a tighter network (larger V_1/V_e) raises the elastic penalty and lowers Q.
explanations.c: Incorrect - Q depends strongly on crosslink density.

questions.question: Q3. A PAA hydrogel is designed to release a drug in the intestine but not the stomach. Which behaviour enables this?

answers.a: It swells in acid (stomach) and collapses in alkaline (intestine).
answers.b: It collapses in acid (stomach, pH ~2) and swells in alkaline (intestine, pH ~7), releasing the drug there.
answers.c: It dissolves completely at any pH.

explanations.a: Incorrect - the behaviour is the opposite for a polyacid.
explanations.b: Correct - a polyacid is collapsed and protective in acid and swells to release in alkaline conditions.
explanations.c: Incorrect - a crosslinked gel does not dissolve.

questions.question: Q4. The Volume Change Ratio (VCR) of PNIPAM across its LCST is typically 20-40x. Why is this significant for 4D actuators?

answers.a: It is smaller than any other material, so PNIPAM is rarely used.
answers.b: Such a large reversible volume change enables large-stroke actuation that far exceeds SMP or SMA (~8% strain).
answers.d: It only matters for electrical devices.

explanations.a: Incorrect - the VCR is unusually large, not small.
explanations.b: Correct - the large reversible VCR gives PNIPAM the biggest stroke among common stimulus-responsive materials.
explanations.c: Incorrect - the large VCR is precisely what enables strong actuation.
explanations.d: Incorrect - the actuation is mechanical, not electrical.

questions.question: Q5. The actuation strain is computed as epsilon_act = (Q_swollen^(1/3) - Q_collapsed^(1/3))/Q_swollen^(1/3). Why the cube-root?

answers.a: Because strain is a volume, not a length.
answers.b: Because linear dimension scales as the cube root of volume, so the cube root converts a volume ratio into a length change.
answers.c: Because cube roots are easier to compute.

explanations.a: Incorrect - strain is a relative length change.
explanations.b: Correct - L is proportional to V^(1/3), so linear strain uses the cube root of the volume ratio.
explanations.c: Incorrect - convenience is not the reason.
explanations.d: Incorrect - the gel is three-dimensional, which is why the cube root appears.

questions.question: Q6. As a hydrogel swells (Q increases), its swollen Young's modulus E:

answers.a: Increases, because more water makes it stiffer.
answers.b: Decreases, because G_swollen = G_dry / Q^(1/3) dilutes the load-bearing strands.

explanations.a: Incorrect - water dilutes the network and softens it.
explanations.b: Correct - swelling reduces strand density, lowering G and E (E = 3G).
explanations.d: Incorrect - modulus decreases, it does not diverge.

questions.question: Q7. The Korsmeyer-Peppas model is only valid for M_t/M_inf < 0.6. What happens beyond this cutoff?

answers.a: The drug is fully released and nothing more can be modelled.
answers.b: The finite-reservoir condition is violated, so the power-law fit and any t-extrapolation become unreliable.

explanations.a: Incorrect - release continues beyond 60% but the model no longer applies.
explanations.b: Correct - beyond ~60% the infinite-reservoir assumption fails, so the fit must be restricted to early data.
explanations.c: Incorrect - n is a fitted constant, not forced to 1.
explanations.d: Incorrect - there is no sudden doubling.

questions.question: Q8. Rubber elasticity (G = nu_e k_B T) becomes inaccurate at very high swelling (Q > 50). Why?

answers.b: Because the network strands approach full extension and leave the Gaussian regime, requiring a non-Gaussian (Arruda-Boyce) model.
answers.c: Because the gel turns into a metal.

explanations.a: Incorrect - temperature still appears in the law.
explanations.b: Correct - highly swollen strands are nearly fully stretched, so Gaussian statistics fail and the 8-chain model is needed.
explanations.c: Incorrect - the material remains a polymer.
explanations.d: Incorrect - the Boltzmann constant is fixed.

questions.question: Q9. A designer needs a scaffold matching cartilage (E = 0.1-1 MPa). Which adjustment moves a too-stiff gel into this window?

answers.a: Increase crosslink density to raise nu_e.
answers.b: Increase the swelling ratio Q (or lower crosslink density) to soften the gel.
answers.c: Lower the temperature to absolute zero.

explanations.a: Incorrect - raising nu_e makes the gel stiffer, moving away from the target.
explanations.b: Correct - more swelling lowers E via E = 3 G_dry / Q^(1/3), softening the gel toward the tissue range.
explanations.c: Incorrect - that is not physically practical and only scales G linearly.
explanations.d: Incorrect - drug loading does not set the modulus.

questions.question: Q10. For an ionic gel, the correct modelling workflow in this lab is:

answers.a: Use Sub-Calc A alone, since Flory-Rehner already includes charge effects.
answers.b: Compute the Flory-Rehner result (Sub-Calc A) and then add the Donnan osmotic correction (Sub-Calc B).

explanations.a: Incorrect - classical Flory-Rehner has no electrostatic term.
explanations.b: Correct - the ionic correction from the Donnan term must be added to the non-ionic Flory-Rehner result.
explanations.c: Incorrect - swelling is the central quantity.
explanations.d: Incorrect - drug release does not determine equilibrium swelling.
